For the last assertion, deleting a bridge outside the paths while
retaining its attachments preserves $\Psi_1$ and gives a toroidal
proper minor of $G$. Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test} then gives a passing
choice.
\end{proof}

Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant} handles three-attachment bridges
with a planar relevant completion. If a bridge has none,
the next corollary of Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test} and minor-minimality shows that it is the only bridge and that
every path outside it is an edge.

\begin{corollary}\label{dis:lone-bridge}
If a bridge $B$ has no planar relevant completion, then $G=\Psi_1\cup B$ and
the paths not in $B$ are edges.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
If $\Psi_1\cup B$ were toroidal,
Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test} would give a planar relevant
completion of $B$, contrary to the hypothesis. Thus
$\Psi_1\cup B$ is nontoroidal, so $G=\Psi_1\cup B$ by
minimality. An internal vertex of a path not contained
in $B$ would then have degree two in $G$, contrary to
three-connectivity. Hence every such path is an edge.
\end{proof}


When every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion, the
preceding results give finitely many possible forms for the
bridges. Each three-attachment bridge has either one interior
vertex or one of the forms in
Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}. Each four-attachment
bridge has one interior vertex, and at most three have the
same attachment set, since four would give a $K_{4,4}$ subgraph
and hence a $K_5$ minor. We combine these forms with disjoint
interiors, subject to the attachment restrictions and
Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}. A bridge containing $P_m$ includes
both that path and all $\Psi_1$-bridges meeting its interior,
so listing its possible forms also accounts for the length
of $P_m$. The resulting enumerations are recorded
in~\supp{E4,~E5}.

$T(c_1),T(c_2),T(h),S(c_1;c_2),S(c_2;c_1)$. For a bridge containing $P_m$ on one
of the twelve triples containing $s_m,t_m$, also allow
$Q(h;g,e)$ and the two four-cycle
forms of Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical}, with $g,e,h$
as in Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant} and in the roles of $x,y,z$.
These choices give $18\cdot6+12\cdot3=144$ labeled
three-attachment forms. Each bridge is chosen independently,
subject to the bounds below.

\item The four-attachment bridges have one interior vertex,
on one of the three sets $\{s_i,t_i,s_j,t_j\}$ or the six sets
$\{s_m,t_m,s_x,t_y\}$ with $\{m,x,y\}=\{1,2,3\}$.
The latter are of type (c). Together with the nine possible
edges, this gives $144+9+9=162$ labeled edge and bridge types.

\item Count all forms on the same attachment set together.
By Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}, at most three bridges use any
one triple, except that four are allowed when it contains
$s_m,t_m$ and $s_mt_m$ is absent, allowing for the bridge
containing $P_m$. At most three single vertices use any
one set $\{s_i,t_i,s_j,t_j\}$, since four give a $K_{4,4}$ subgraph
and hence a $K_5$ minor. For each $m$, at most one bridge
among the $Q$, four-cycle and type (c) forms associated
with $P_m$ is included, and its presence requires
$s_mt_m$ to be absent.
\end{enumerate}

We exclude adjacent neighbors at a degree-three interior
vertex and simultaneous edges $s_it_j,s_jt_i$ for $i\ne j$,
by Lemmas~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a)
and~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. For each absent edge
$s_mt_m$, some bridge must have both ends among its attachments.
The construction does not mark the paths or require their
simultaneous disjoint realization, so it also includes
additional graphs. Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant},
Corollary~\ref{dis:remaining-completions}, Proposition~\ref{dis:types}
and the bounds above place every graph under consideration
in this finite family.

By \eqref{dis:shortest}, some edge $s_mt_m$ is absent.

the formula.variables: Variable vj of atom A<i> (its list [v1, ..., vm]) means "at least j copies of A<i>". Variables after 456 are auxiliary (cardinality counters).
the formula.base clauses: 6483 clauses: v(j+1) implies vj for each atom, then the constraints of the case listed below.
the formula.one clause per recorded graph: For a toroidal graph with n_i copies of A<i>: the clause that some atom has more copies than in it. For a nontoroidal graph: the clause that some atom in it has fewer copies.

what this shows: Every assembly allowed by the base clauses either lies inside a recorded toroidal graph, so it is toroidal, or contains a recorded nontoroidal graph. An obstruction of the case therefore equals a recorded nontoroidal graph in the family, and the verdicts of those give the stated list.
not in this item: The recorded nontoroidal graphs come with no certificate of nontoroidality here; their genus computations are part of the table of genus computations cited in Appendix A.
